findings.claim: Adding `QUERY` only to this `If-None-Match: *` branch likely leaves the rest of the middleware inconsistent about the QUERY method.
findings.rationale: The etag middleware typically gates other behavior on the request method as well (e.g. whether an ETag is generated/attached at all, or which responses are eligible for 304 / cache handling elsewhere in this file or in the cache middleware). If those checks still only list GET/HEAD, a QUERY request can now receive a 304 in the `*` case while never getting an ETag header (or vice-versa) in the ordinary flow, producing asymmetric behavior. Worth verifying every `method === 'GET' || method === 'HEAD'` site in the package and factoring them into one shared predicate/set. Medium confidence — depends on code outside this hunk.

findings.claim: The non-`*` branch (`etagMatches`) still applies to any method, so the new method allow-list is only enforced for `If-None-Match: *`.
findings.rationale: Per RFC 9110, `If-None-Match` on a non-safe method that fails should yield 412, and 304 is only valid for GET/HEAD (now GET/HEAD/QUERY). Here a POST/PUT with a concrete `If-None-Match` value that matches will still be turned into a 304 below. This is pre-existing rather than introduced by the diff, but the change draws attention to the asymmetry and is a good time to align both branches on the same method predicate. Moderate confidence about the spec mismatch, low confidence it's in scope for this change.

findings.claim: Method comparison uses raw uppercase string literals; a lowercase or non-normalized `c.req.method` would silently skip the QUERY case.
findings.rationale: Hono normally surfaces `method` exactly as sent by the client/runtime; HTTP methods are case-sensitive so uppercase comparison is technically correct, but if any adapter (test harness, custom fetch mock) passes `query`, the branch quietly falls through to a full 200 response instead of 304. Low confidence this matters in practice, but using a shared constant/set of allowed methods would make it robust and self-documenting.
